questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “The @extend Rule” in Dart Sass?
options: Advanced at-rules change how styles are emitted or how selectors are combined. Inspect their effect on the final selector list rather than deciding only from how concise the SCSS looks.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.
questions.answer_key: Advanced at-rules change how styles are emitted or how selectors are combined. Inspect their effect on the final selector list rather than deciding only from how concise the SCSS looks.
questions.explanation: Advanced at-rules change how styles are emitted or how selectors are combined. Inspect their effect on the final selector list rather than deciding only from how concise the SCSS looks. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Introduction to selector extension”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
Predict the expanded selector before compiling. Keep nesting shallow and verify that the emitted selector does not match more elements than intended.
questions.answer_key: Predict the expanded selector before compiling. Keep nesting shallow and verify that the emitted selector does not match more elements than intended.
questions.explanation: Predict the expanded selector before compiling. Keep nesting shallow and verify that the emitted selector does not match more elements than intended. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.
